chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Salma (the companion of Al-Sabiri), from Abu Al-Sabbah Al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:
For the fasting one there are two joys: a joy at the time of his breaking the fast, and a joy at the time of meeting his Lord.
ai.seo_question: What are the two joys of a fasting person according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This well-known hadith from al-Kafi underscores the dual nature of fasting as both a physical discipline and a spiritual journey, linking the immediate sensory joy of iftar with the eschatological joy of standing before God. In Shia scholarship, this is often interpreted to show that the bodily act of abstention prepares the soul for the ultimate encounter, making the physical experience a precursor to spiritual fulfillment. It serves as a motivational framework for believers, balancing worldly satisfaction with eternal reward.
